lead: Quiet day: the clearest operational signal is better visibility into how gateway session affinity affects provider routing, cache use and per-session cost. That is useful evidence for debugging and cost attribution, but not a substitute for workload-level quality or residency checks. Two OpenAI SDK releases add typed live-session events, an agent service tier and realtime translation sessions; the notes do not state their pricing or availability boundaries. Keep gateway and SDK trials tied to a specific observability or integration gap, and design web agents on the assumption that external services may deny access.

items.title: AI Gateway logs now show session affinity
items.summary: Vercel added a Sessions view that groups AI Gateway requests and shows affinity routing, client, model, provider, cache use, cost, duration and per-turn timing. Session affinity is on by default for text and chat requests; teams can group turns with a shared session ID or header, while requests without one are grouped using a conversation-opening fingerprint; pricing and regional availability are not stated.
items.so_what: Trial the session view against your existing traces and cost dashboards to see whether it improves attribution of provider changes and cache behaviour; check what the fingerprinting approach means for your telemetry and privacy controls.

items.title: v3.35.0
items.summary: OpenAI Python SDK v3.35.0, dated 17 October 2026, adds typed Live sideband events and an ultrafast service tier for Agents, plus a fix for byte receives with websockets 13. The release notes do not specify service-tier pricing, eligibility, model coverage or regions.
items.so_what: Trial typed sideband events if your live-session integration needs stronger event handling; compare the service tier only after confirming its eligibility, cost and latency behaviour for your workload.

items.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
items.summary: The Verge reports that services including Delta Air Lines, JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab block some third-party agents from booking or accessing accounts, citing security concerns and service policies. It also describes anti-bot systems and unresolved legal disputes as practical constraints on browser-agent access; this is secondary reporting and does not quantify how often access fails.
items.so_what: Design browser-agent workflows with explicit service permission, graceful denial and a user-controlled fallback; do not make access to external sites a production assumption.

items.title: v3.34.0
items.summary: OpenAI Python SDK v3.34.0, dated 17 October 2026, adds a degraded external-storage status and Realtime Translation WebSocket sessions. The release note does not describe supported providers or regions, pricing, or the operational semantics of the degraded-storage status.
items.so_what: Trial the storage-status signal in your failure handling and assess the translation session integration only against a defined enterprise use case; confirm service boundaries before relying on either in production.
